agents.task:
Perform comprehensive reconnaissance and attack-surface mapping of the in-scope black-box target: https://petcare-udee.onrender.com (ONLY this host — never test other domains/IPs).

Deliverables:
1. Technology fingerprinting: frameworks, server, languages, JS libraries, versions (headers, cookies, HTML source, /robots.txt, sitemap.xml, common files).
2. Full endpoint inventory: crawl all pages (unauthenticated first; if login/registration is available, register a test account and crawl authenticated surfaces too). Use katana/gospider with bounded depth, plus a bounded ffuf/dirsearch pass for hidden paths (common wordlists, limited threads, stop on errors). Analyze all JS files for API endpoints, hidden routes, hardcoded secrets/API keys.
3. Map authentication & session model: login/register/logout endpoints, cookie/token type, session cookie names, any JWT usage, roles visible in UI.
4. Inventory all parameters, forms, and API endpoints with methods, and note which require auth and which don't.
5. Save a durable summary note (create_note, category "wiki" or "general") with: tech stack, endpoint list (method + path + auth required Y/N + parameters), session model, and any interesting observations. Also call save_threat_model on https://petcare-udee.onrender.com with a black-box derived threat model (mark inferred vs observed).
6. Record coverage entries (record_coverage) for surfaces you mapped.

Constraints: keep scans bounded (no aggressive directory brute forcing beyond common wordlists; throttle), do not run exploitation payloads yet — this phase is mapping only. Do not use identifiable markers in requests. Clean up large raw output files from /workspace once endpoint lists are extracted.

When done, call agent_finish with a concise completion summary.

You are a second recon agent working in parallel with a primary mapping agent on the in-scope black-box target: https://petcare-udee.onrender.com (ONLY this host — never test other domains/IPs).

Your EXCLUSIVE focus: the authentication, registration, and user-account surface. Do NOT do general crawling or directory bruteforcing (the primary recon agent covers that).

Deliverables:
1. Map the full auth flows: register, login, logout, password reset, profile/account management, session handling. Use the agent-browser CLI (via exec_command, always with `--session authrecon`) to drive the UI — register a fresh test account, log in, log out, inspect cookies and tokens in the browser and via Caido proxy captures (list_requests/view_request).
2. Characterize the session model precisely: cookie names, attributes (HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite), JWT tokens if any (decode header/payload, note signing algorithm, expiry, claims), where tokens are stored (cookie vs localStorage), how requests authenticate (header vs cookie).
3. Note any visible roles/admin surfaces, user enumeration signals on login/register (distinguishable error messages, response timing), and password policy.
4. Write findings to a shared note (create_note, category "general", tags ["auth-recon","endpoints"]) so other agents build on it. Do not write a threat model (primary agent owns that).
5. Record coverage entries (record_coverage) for the auth surfaces you assess.

Constraints: mapping only — do NOT attempt exploitation (no auth bypass, no password brute force, no payload injection). Throttle requests. No identifiable markers in requests/usernames (use plausible generic names). Clean up raw output files.

When done, call agent_finish with a concise completion summary.
